title: Q12 v3: orchestrator/jev_planner.py — Jev as a shadow routing signal for Planner tier choice: typed batched questions over redacted structured state, fail open, never bypasses hard escalation (P12)
spec:
Why: the brief (P12) allows Jev to provide probabilistic decision characteristics to the Planner router, shadow first, as a signal and never as authority. jev_points.py (T-0586) shows the pattern: typed options, redacted evidence, mode per point, fail open. Nothing asks Jev about Planner routing. Spec reviews T-0687 and of T-0694 are folded in: classification producer, explicit state_version, signals source, cache rows, classification fingerprint in the cache key, task parameter, jev_mode source, confidence aggregation, availability shape.
What: new module orchestrator/jev_planner.py; jev.ask injected as ask_fn so tests never hit the network. Inputs are dicts read with .get(): classification = planner_taxonomy.classify output (orchestrator/planner_taxonomy.py on goal/T-0674: decision_type, architectural, ambiguous, risk_class, signals list[str], band, task_class); ctx = decision.route's ctx dict; goal and task = bus task dicts (task None for goal-level decisions). cfg = the dict returned by planner_router.load_cfg(pool_cfg) (Q4 v3 T-0700, same goal): this module reads only cfg.get("jev_mode", "shadow") from it; pool.toml wiring is [planner.routing].jev_mode. availability has the router contract shape {tier: {"available": bool, "reason": str}, "fable_reserve_ok": bool} and is built by planner_runs in Wave B; should_ask counts tiers whose value is a dict with available True.
- QUESTIONS = OrderedDict of five typed yes/no questions keyed routine_localized, architectural_reasoning, requirements_ambiguous, long_horizon, fable_improves_outcome, one sentence each.
- subject(goal, task) -> the task dict when task is not None else goal (mirrors classify's task-over-goal preference for held_task/fix_strategy/architectural_replan).
- state(classification, ctx, goal, task=None) -> bounded redacted dict: decision_type, band, task_class, architectural, risk_class from classification; signals = classification signals[:10], each jev.redact'ed and capped 100 chars; subject_id, subject_title = jev.redact(subject title)[:200], spec_excerpt = jev.redact(first 300 chars of subject spec), goal_title = jev.redact(goal title)[:200]; scope_count = len(subject scope); scout_count, failing_test_count (len(ctx failing_ids)), spec_review_request_changes, auto_fix_rounds_used, signature_repeated from ctx. Never file contents, diffs or review comment bodies; json.dumps(state) <= 4000 chars, truncating spec_excerpt then signals until it fits.
- fingerprint(classification) -> sha256(json.dumps({decision_type, risk_class, architectural, band, task_class}, sort_keys=True))[:12].
- should_ask(router_mode, jev_mode, hard_reasons, availability, route) -> (bool, reason): False with jev_off (jev_mode == "off"), hard_decision (hard_reasons non-empty), single_tier (fewer than two available tiers), deterministic (route name != "escalate"), cannot_affect (router_mode == "off"); else (True, "eligible"). Shadow and active both ask; applying the signal is the router's job.
- ask(classification, ctx, goal, *, cfg, router_mode, hard_reasons, availability, route, state_version, task=None, ask_fn=jev.ask, cache=None, root=None) -> {"asked": bool, "reason", "mode": jev_mode, "signals": {key: float|None}, "soft_adjust": float, "confidence": float|None, "cached": bool}. One ask_fn(state, questions, task=subject id) call carrying all five questions. Each answer parsed as jev_points._answer does: probability float(answer["noul"]) in [0, 1] else None, confidence answer.get("confidence"); confidence = None if any per-question confidence is None else their mean. soft_adjust = clamp(0.2 * mean(p_architectural, p_ambiguous, p_long_horizon, p_fable) - 0.2 * p_routine, -0.2, 0.2); ask_fn returning None -> asked True, reason jev_unavailable, soft_adjust 0.0, signals all None; unparsable answers -> reason jev_malformed, soft_adjust 0.0. cache: dict keyed (goal id, state_version, fingerprint(classification)); a hit returns the cached result with cached True and no ask_fn call; a changed risk_class or architectural under the same state_version misses. Every call (asked, skipped or cached) appends one row via schedlog.append("planner_jev", {goal_id, subject_id, decision_type, state_version, fingerprint, asked, cached, reason, signals, soft_adjust, confidence, mode}) with no question text and no state text.
- summary(root=None) -> {"n", "asked", "cached", "skip_reasons": dict, "mean_soft_adjust"} via schedlog.read_with_malformed, tolerant of malformed lines.
acceptance: tests/test_jev_planner.py::test_off_and_hard_and_single_tier_never_ask — jev_mode off, hard_reasons ['security'], one available tier and a routine route each give asked False with the documented reason, no ask_fn call, and still one planner_jev row

tests/test_jev_planner.py::test_batched_single_call_soft_adjust_and_confidence — exactly one ask_fn call carries five questions; noul 1.0 for architectural/ambiguous/long_horizon/fable and 0 routine give soft_adjust 0.2; all routine gives -0.2; never outside [-0.2, 0.2]; confidence is the mean of five confidences and None when one is missing

tests/test_jev_planner.py::test_malformed_and_timeout_fail_open — ask_fn returning None and ask_fn returning {'answers': 'garbage'} both yield soft_adjust 0.0 with reasons jev_unavailable / jev_malformed, and a row is recorded

tests/test_jev_planner.py::test_state_is_redacted_bounded_and_task_scoped — a task spec with a token-like secret and 20k chars and a classification with 30 signals yields spec_excerpt <= 300 chars taken from the task (not the goal), at most 10 signals, the secret redacted, no key named diff/contents/comments, json <= 4000 chars, and decision_type/band/risk_class copied from the classification

tests/test_jev_planner.py::test_cache_key_includes_classification_fingerprint — a second ask with the same goal, state_version and classification returns cached True with zero extra ask_fn calls and appends a row with cached True; the same state_version with risk_class changed to high asks again; summary counts asked, cached and skip reasons over rows including one malformed line

constraints.interface_contract: should_ask(router_mode, jev_mode, hard_reasons, availability, route) -> (bool, reason); ask(classification, ctx, goal, *, cfg, router_mode, hard_reasons, availability, route, state_version, task=None, ask_fn=jev.ask, cache=None, root=None) -> {asked, reason, mode, signals, soft_adjust in [-0.2, 0.2], confidence, cached}; fingerprint(classification) -> str; cfg = planner_router.load_cfg(pool_cfg) dict, key jev_mode (pool.toml [planner.routing].jev_mode); classification = planner_taxonomy.classify dict; caller passes state_version = planner_runs.state_version(goal_id) and the held task as task; the router consumes soft_adjust as jev_signal and ignores it for hard decisions; rows in runs/sched/planner_jev.jsonl.

result.summary: superseded by Q12 v4 after spec review request_changes round 3 (subject_id in the cache key; ambiguous in the fingerprint; router citation clarified). Planner decision: the v4 spec review is waived after three rounds with every risk folded in (precedent decisions.md 2026-09-18 C-O3/C-O4), v4 dispatches directly.

spec_review_risks.issue: Cache key is (goal_id, state_version, fingerprint(classification)) with no subject id. For 'held' decisions, subject(goal, task) is the task, but state_version hashes over ALL of a goal's child tasks together. Two different held execute tasks under the same goal can share an identical state_version (nothing else changed) and an identical fingerprint (same decision_type/risk_class/architectural/band/task_class, since fingerprint doesn't include the task itself), causing task B's ask() to return task A's cached soft_adjust/signals/confidence -- a wrong-subject answer silently reused, and cached=True logged against the wrong subject_id in the planner_jev row. The acceptance test only varies risk_class on a single subject, so it doesn't catch this. Add subject_id (task id when present, else goal id) to the cache key tuple.

fingerprint() hashes {decision_type, risk_class, architectural, band, task_class} but omits classification['ambiguous']. For 'held' kind decisions, planner_taxonomy.classify only folds ambiguous into decision_type for initial_goal_plan/scout_results, so held_task/fix_strategy/architectural_replan can be ambiguous=True or False while keeping the same fingerprint -- compounding the cache-collision risk above and blurring the requirements_ambiguous signal the cache is supposed to preserve per-state.

The spec's 'What' section cites the router config source as '(Q4 v3 T-0700, same goal)'. plan.md's actual decomposition has planner_router.py as Q4 T-0680, not T-0700; T-0700 doesn't exist as a task or branch in this repo. Wrong dependency citation could mislead a reader checking whether the prerequisite has landed, even though jev_planner.py itself takes cfg as a caller-supplied parameter rather than importing planner_router directly.
